channel.title: The Art Newspaper - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Art Newspaper (theartnewspaper.com)

item.title: Are we seeing the demise of statement stands at art fairs?
item.description: The waning adventurousness in these spaces speaks to important shifts in the trade over the past two decades

item.title: How four Los Angeles artists are doing a year after the wildfires
item.description: Kelly Akashi, Christina Quarles, Adam Ross and Kathryn Andrews, all of whom lost their homes in the Eaton and Palisades fires, reflect on the last year

item.title: Is it finally time for the Guerrilla Girls to remove their masks?
item.description: A new Getty show on the activists’ legacy points to the power and limits of anonymity

item.title: A selective history of the moving image comes to downtown Los Angeles
item.description: The Germany-based Julia Stoschek Foundation, which has an unmatched collection of time-based works spanning the 1960s to now, presents its first major US exhibition at Variety Arts Theater

item.title: 'If a work is meant to be mine, there’s always time': Mashonda Tifrere on the art she collects and why
item.description: The singer-turned-curator, and founder of two non-profits focused on uplifting women and underrepresented artists, shares her enthusiasm for Hiba Schahbaz’s paintings and her Oscars picks

item.title: Why Robert Therrien is a big deal
item.description: A posthumous retrospective of the Los Angeles conceptual artist’s work at The Broad includes his famous large-scale sculptures of everyday objects, and much more

item.title: Bearing the weight of the world: Amanda Ross-Ho rolls out a new performance at Frieze Los Angeles
item.description: The artist embraces the Sisyphean task of clocking the fair’s duration on its three-acre turf field

item.title: Los Angeles museums on the cusp of new golden age
item.description: Could the city’s cultural cachet soon match that of New York? A slew of multi-million-dollar projects, from dramatic new museums to major renovations, suggest that it could

item.title: ‘Painting continues to be viable’: Enrique Martínez Celaya on his sugar-coated show at the Wende Museum
item.description: The Los Angeles-based artist’s new show is inspired by his Cold War-era childhood in Cuba, and the final entry in a trilogy of exhibitions

item.title: Palisades Fire Memorial rises from the ashes
item.description: A project organised by the House Museum aims to preserve the chimneys of architecturally significant homes that were destroyed in last year’s catastrophic blazes
